content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To put on a dog harness, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Untangle the nylon chest straps (45 seconds)
Step 2. Buckle the final safety latch (10 seconds)
Step 3. Guide the dog's left paw through the loop (15 seconds)
Step 4. Locate the harness in the storage bin (1 minute)
Step 5. Reward the dog with a small treat for staying still (30 seconds)
Step 6. Tighten the shoulder sliders for a snug fit (2 minutes)
Step 7. Check the girth strap for two-finger clearance (20 seconds)
Step 8. Align the back D-ring with the spine (15 seconds)
Step 9. Shake out the harness to see the orientation (10 seconds)
Step 10. Position the chest plate centrally (30 seconds)
Step 11. Lift the front of the harness over the dog's head (20 seconds)
Step 12. Calm the dog with gentle petting (2 minutes)
Step 13. Inspect the straps for any twists (30 seconds)
Step 14. Identify the neck opening (10 seconds)
Step 15. Call the dog over to the grooming area (1 minute)
Step 16. Lay the harness flat on the floor (40 seconds)
Step 17. Verify the belly strap is not upside down (15 seconds)
Step 18. Open all the quick-release buckles (30 seconds)
Step 19. Retrieve the dog's favorite training treats (2 minutes)
Step 20. Double-check the harness size setting (1 minute)
Step 21. Wipe down the dog's underside if muddy (2 minutes)
Step 22. Remove the harness from its packaging (1 minute)
Step 23. Check the reflective stitching for wear (1 minute)
Step 24. Clear the workspace of obstacles (3 minutes)
Step 25. Read the manufacturer's instruction card (5 minutes)
Step 26. Distinguish the top side from the bottom side (20 seconds)
Step 27. Ensure the logo is facing outward (10 seconds)
Step 28. Brush the dog's coat to prevent matting under straps (5 minutes)
Step 29. Gather all necessary walking gear (4 minutes)
Step 30. Straighten the under-belly connector (30 seconds)
Step 31. Check for any pinched fur in the clips (15 seconds)
Step 32. Loosen the adjustment points to maximum width (45 seconds)
Step 33. Ensure the buckle prongs are clean (10 seconds)
Step 34. Command the dog to "sit" and "stay" (30 seconds)
Step 35. Center the harness over the shoulders (20 seconds)
Step 36. Remove the dog's standard house collar (20 seconds)
Step 37. Clip the leash to the metal D-ring (10 seconds)
Step 38. Identify the "left" and "right" labels (15 seconds)
Step 39. Wash your hands before handling the gear (40 seconds)
Step 40. Snap the first side buckle into place (15 seconds)
Step 41. Tuck away any excess strap length (30 seconds)
Step 42. Smooth out the padding against the dog's skin (25 seconds)
Step 43. Check the weather to decide on a fleece liner (1 minute)
Step 44. Position yourself behind the dog (15 seconds)
Step 45. Give the "let's go" command (5 seconds)
Step 46. Slide the neck loop down to the base of the neck (15 seconds)
Step 47. Encourage the dog with a happy tone (10 seconds)
Step 48. Hold the harness by the top handle (15 seconds)
Step 49. Snap the second side buckle into place (15 seconds)
Step 50. Clear a path to the front door (2 minutes)
Step 51. Inspect the harness for any frayed edges or damage (2 minutes)
Step 52. Offer a piece of kibble to keep the dog's focus (10 seconds)
Step 53. Perform a final "tug test" on all connections (10 seconds)
Step 54. Calm the dog's excitement with a "down" command (1 minute)
Step 55. Adjust the sternum strap length (40 seconds)
Step 56. Guide the dog's right paw through the second loop (15 seconds)
Step 57. Check that the "Y" shape is oriented correctly (20 seconds)
Step 58. Pull the belly section forward between the legs (20 seconds)
Step 59. Lift the harness slightly to clear the dog's elbows (15 seconds)
Step 60. Put on your own walking shoes (3 minutes)
Step 61. Ensure the dog's ears are not caught in the neck hole (10 seconds)
Step 62. Check that you have poop bags in your pocket (30 seconds)
Step 63. Untwist the main girth webbing (25 seconds)
Step 64. Take the harness out of the closet (15 seconds)
Step 65. Verify that the harness is not obstructing leg movement (30 seconds)
Step 66. Brush the dog's chest area (1 minute)
Step 67. Put on your jacket (2 minutes)
Step 68. Grab the house keys (15 seconds)
Step 69. Make sure the harness isn't too tight around the armpits (20 seconds)
Step 70. Open the front door (10 seconds)
